refs.quote: INDICATIONS AND USAGE Bisoprolol fumarate tablets are indicated in the management of hypertension. It may be used alone or in combination with other antihypertensive agents.

The usual starting dose is 5 mg once daily. In some patients, 2.5 mg may be an appropriate starting dose (see Bronchospastic Disease in WARNINGS ). If the antihypertensive effect of 5 mg is inadequate, the dose may be increased to 10 mg and then, if necessary, to 20 mg once daily.

refs.quote: In patients with hepatic impairment (hepatitis or cirrhosis) or renal dysfunction (creatinine clearance less than 40 mL/min), the initial daily dose should be 2.5 mg and caution should be used in dose-titration.

In patients with cirrhosis of the liver, the elimination of bisoprolol fumarate tablets is more variable in rate and significantly slower than that in healthy subjects, with plasma half-life ranging from 8.3 to 21.7 hours.

Bisoprolol fumarate tablets are a beta 1 -selective (cardioselective) adrenoceptor blocking agent without significant membrane stabilizing activity or intrinsic sympathomimetic activity in its therapeutic dosage range.

mechanism_of_action.value: Synthetic, beta-1 selective (cardioselective) adrenoceptor blocking agent without significant membrane stabilizing activity or intrinsic sympathomimetic activity in its therapeutic dosage range; at higher doses (>= 20 mg) it also inhibits beta-2 adrenoceptors. Antihypertensive mechanisms may include decreased cardiac output, inhibition of renal renin release, and diminution of tonic sympathetic outflow.

refs.quote: Bisoprolol fumarate tablets are a beta 1 -selective (cardioselective) adrenoceptor blocking agent without significant membrane stabilizing activity or intrinsic sympathomimetic activity in its therapeutic dosage range. Cardioselectivity is not absolute, however, and at higher doses (≥ 20 mg) bisoprolol fumarate also inhibits beta 2 -adrenoceptors
Bisoprolol fumarate is eliminated equally by renal and non-renal pathways with about 50% of the dose appearing unchanged in the urine and the remainder appearing in the form of inactive metabolites.

enzyme_profile.note: Eliminated equally by renal (50% unchanged) and non-renal hepatic pathways; not metabolized by CYP2D6.

tier.note: No adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Animal studies showed no teratogenicity up to high multiples of MRHD, but fetotoxicity (increased late resorptions in rats at 50 mg/kg/day) and embryolethality (increased early resorptions in rabbits at 12.5 mg/kg/day) occurred. Label advises use during pregnancy only if potential benefit justifies potential risk to the fetus.

refs.quote: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Bisoprolol fumarate tablets should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
Bisoprolol fumarate was fetotoxic (increased late resorptions) at 50 mg/kg/day and maternotoxic (decreased food intake and body weight gain) at 150 mg/kg/day.

lactation_summary.value: It is not known whether bisoprolol is excreted in human milk (small amounts < 2% of dose detected in lactating rat milk); exercise caution when administered to nursing women.

refs.locator: 8 USE IN SPECIFIC POPULATIONS - Nursing Mothers
refs.quote: Small amounts of bisoprolol fumarate (< 2% of the dose) have been detected in the milk of lactating rats. It is not known whether this drug is excreted in human milk. Because many drugs are excreted in human milk caution should be exercised when bisoprolol fumarate is administered to nursing women.
